trade-surplus.reason: A trade balance is a poor target on its own; what matters is whether people can afford what they need and produce something worthwhile.

population-transfer.reason: Pushing out a minority is a grave rights violation, and calling it protection does not change that.

initiating-force-wrong.reason: I hold the principle firmly, though I think defence and answering aggression are the main justified exceptions.

competition-drives-progress.reason: Rivalry does spur innovation, but institutions and cooperation account for at least as much of lasting progress.

ban-extremist-parties.reason: Banning parties that would dismantle democracy has real precedent, but the bar for it has to be high and it is easy to abuse.

freedom-as-non-domination.reason: Living at the mercy of someone who can interfere arbitrarily is a real loss of freedom even if they never act.

separated-powers.reason: Dividing power among bodies that can check each other is one of the most reliable safeguards against abuse I know of.

vanguard-party.reason: Workers can organize and set their own aims, and a leading party risks replacing their judgment with its own.

priority-to-poor.reason: Attention to the poorest matters, but equal treatment under law is also a value I weigh heavily, so I am torn.

right-to-buy-council-homes.reason: Selling off public housing tends to shrink the stock for those who most need it, and I think that cost is often underweighted.

restrict-strikes-picketing.reason: Ballots before strikes seem reasonable to me, but tight limits on picketing would weaken a basic bargaining tool.

population-causes-poverty.reason: Population pressure matters in some places, but the evidence points more to institutions and property arrangements as the main drivers.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.reason: Trust can be harder to build across groups, but diversity does not inherently weaken a society and often brings real strengths.

offices-by-lottery.reason: Sortition can suit some advisory or jury-like bodies, but I think accountable elections are better for choosing governing officials.

emergency-suspend-protections.reason: Emergencies are exactly when legal protections matter most, and suspending them invites the abuses they exist to prevent.

price-controls-essentials.reason: Short-term ceilings can protect people in a crisis, but they usually bring shortages, so I see real trade-offs.

party-controls-media.reason: A free press and open internet are essential to accountability, and government control of them removes that check.

party-commands-army.reason: An army loyal to a party rather than to the state and constitution is a serious threat to democratic government.

long-naturalization-wait.reason: Some residence requirement is reasonable, but I think very long waits are harder to justify than the goal of integration requires.

representatives-worker-pay.reason: Modest pay for officials has real appeal, but tying it to the average wage risks deterring capable people from public service.

party-discipline-binding.reason: Parties need some discipline to function, but I think members should keep room to act on conscience in serious matters.

pool-sovereignty.reason: Shared institutions can solve problems no single country can handle alone, provided they remain accountable to the people they bind.

head-commands-forces.reason: Putting the military and the cabinet under one executive without legislative control removes a core check on power.

church-by-bishops.reason: How a church governs itself is for its own members to decide, so I would rather not take a side.

clerical-rule.reason: Giving religious scholars the final say over the state takes political power away from citizens and their elected representatives.

defeat-own-government-war.reason: Solidarity across borders is a serious value, but I think ordinary people in a war can reasonably oppose their rulers without wanting their country defeated.

censor-art-for-virtue.reason: Authorities deciding which art and stories shape character is a dangerous power, and free expression matters more to me.

unlimited-reelection.reason: Term limits exist because leaders tend to entrench themselves, and removing them weakens a basic safeguard.

recall-officials.reason: Letting voters remove officials who have clearly lost their confidence makes representation more accountable.

end-foreign-alliances.reason: Overseas commitments carry costs and risks, but whether they serve security depends heavily on the threats involved.

abolish-rental-housing.reason: Renting is a useful and legitimate arrangement, and banning it would hurt people who need flexibility or cannot buy.

people-in-arms.reason: Citizens can contribute to defence, but a modern state needs trained professional forces to defend itself reliably.

rural-life-healthier.reason: Rural communities have real strengths, but I do not think cities are morally worse, and that claim is hard to support.

reunify-divided-nation.reason: Peoples have a real claim to unity, but stability, consent and the cost of redrawing borders make me hesitant to endorse it as a general rule.

educated-out-of-touch.reason: Some elites do lose touch with everyday life, but attributing that to schooling itself is a generalization I do not accept.

cultures-equal-different.reason: Cultures deserve equal moral respect, though I would still judge particular practices and some historical achievements on their merits.

death-penalty.reason: I lean against executions because of the risk of irreversible error and the state's power over life, though I see the case for the gravest crimes.

sex-ed-in-schools.reason: Age-appropriate teaching about sex and equality helps young people make informed and safe choices.

creationism-in-schools.reason: Presenting creation accounts as science alongside evolution misleads students about what the scientific evidence shows.

restrict-pornography.reason: Protecting children and limiting exploitation justify some rules, but I am reluctant to see adults' lawful choices restricted by the state.

citizenship-by-descent.reason: Both descent and birthright systems have sound arguments, so I do not think either is clearly right.

minority-language-support.reason: Teaching and public services in minority languages help people participate fully, though I am less sure about ballots.

religious-exemptions.reason: Accommodating religious practice matters, but exemptions have to be weighed case by case against the interests general laws protect.

encourage-eccentricity.reason: Individuality matters, but shared customs also hold communities together, so I would not actively encourage unusual ways of living.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.reason: Relief for heavily indebted poor countries can be justified, but treating all such debts as cancellable on principle goes further than I would.

independence-needs-economic-change.reason: Economic dependence does limit what formal independence means, but I think independence has value in its own right.

constituent-assembly.reason: A specially elected assembly can be a legitimate way to write a constitution, but it depends heavily on the circumstances.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.reason: Political freedoms are not a price to trade for growth, and history gives little reason to trust that such limits will be lifted.

rich-countries-aid-poor.reason: Severe poverty is a serious moral claim regardless of where people live, so wealthy countries should give substantial help.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.reason: An independent deterrent offers security, but it carries proliferation risks and costs, so I am torn on it.
